presentingComplaint: Fever with rigors, confusion and reduced urine output for 2 days
history: 2-day history of high-grade fever with rigors on a background of dysuria and increased urinary frequency for a week. Over the last 24 hours family noted drowsiness and mild confusion, poor oral intake and markedly reduced urine output. Type 2 diabetic on metformin, with benign prostatic hyperplasia. No recent hospitalization or antibiotic use in the last 90 days. No known drug allergies.
examination: Ill and toxic-appearing, drowsy but rousable (GCS 14), warm peripheries with flash capillary refill. Left costovertebral angle tenderness and suprapubic tenderness. Chest clear, no meningism, no rash. Pertinent negatives: no neck stiffness, no focal neurology, no cardiac murmur, no calf swelling.

labs.urinalysis: leucocyte esterase +++, nitrites positive, pyuria, WBC >100/hpf

imaging: Bedside renal USS: mild left hydronephrosis, no calculus/obstruction; CXR clear. CT KUB deferred pending stabilisation.
microbiology: Two sets of blood cultures and urine culture sent before antibiotics; Gram-negative bacilli on urine microscopy, cultures pending.
finalDiagnosis: Sepsis secondary to urinary tract source (SOFA increase >=2 with lactate 3.4 and AKI)
stewardship: Empiric IV ceftriaxone 2 g OD (or piperacillin-tazobactam if higher MDR risk) after cultures, with Hour-1 bundle: blood cultures, lactate, 30 mL/kg balanced crystalloid, source control assessment. De-escalate on urine/blood culture sensitivities.
contraindications: Beta-lactam / penicillin allergy (use if no true anaphylaxis history)
Avoid nephrotoxic aminoglycosides as sole agent given AKI
edgeCases: Sepsis can present normothermic or hypothermic and without frank hypotension; warm shock with flash capillary refill may mask hypoperfusion
Elderly/diabetic patients may lack classic localizing signs; confusion may be the only sepsis sign
expectedMaiK: Fever, tachycardia, tachypnea and hypotension with a urinary source plus new AKI, elevated lactate and thrombocytopenia indicate sepsis (life-threatening organ dysfunction from dysregulated host response). Initiate the Hour-1 bundle with cultures, lactate, fluids and empiric guideline-concordant antibiotics; monitor for progression to septic shock.
expectedNextQuestions: Is there ongoing hypotension after fluid resuscitation requiring vasopressors (i.e., evolving septic shock)?
Any recent instrumentation, catheterization, or urinary obstruction requiring source control?
expectedInvestigations: Repeat serum lactate after fluid bolus
Blood and urine cultures with sensitivities
Serial creatinine/urine output and CT KUB to exclude obstructive uropathy

crossAccept.rationale: Septic shock is the severe end of the sepsis continuum; same Surviving-Sepsis bundle.
